text:
If y = y(x) is the solution of the differential equation 

$\frac{dy}{dx}$ + (tan x) y = sin x, $0\leq x\leq \frac{π}{3}$, with y(0) = 0, then $y\left (\frac{π}{4}\right )$ equal to :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 16th March Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Integrating Factor $=e^{\int \tan xdx}=e^{\ln (\sec x)}=\sec x$

$y\sec x=\int (\sin x)\sec xdx=\ln (\sec x)+C$

$y(0)=0\Rightarrow C=0$

$\therefore$ $y=\cos x\ln |\sec x|$

$y\left (\frac{π}{4}\right )=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\ln \left (\sqrt{2}\right )=\frac{1}{2\sqrt{2}}\ln 2$

From (1) & (2)

text:
Let $C_{1}$ be the curve obtained by the solution of differential equation 

$2xy\frac{dy}{dx}=y^{2}-x^{2},x>0$. Let the curve $C_{2}$ be the 

solution of $\frac{2xy}{x^{2}-y^{2}}=\frac{dy}{dx}$. If both the curves pass through (1, 1), then the area enclosed by the curves $C_{1}$ and $C_{2}$ is equal to :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 16th March Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\frac{dy}{dx}=\frac{y^{2}-x^{2}}{2xy}$

Put $y=vx$

$v+x\frac{dv}{dx}=\frac{v^{2}x^{2}-x^{2}}{2vx^{2}}=\frac{v^{2}-1}{2v}$

$x\frac{dv}{dx}=\frac{v^{2}-1-2v^{2}}{2v}=-\frac{(v^{2}+1)}{2v}$

$\Rightarrow \frac{2v}{v^{2}+1}dv=-\frac{dx}{x}$

$\ln (v^{2}+1)=-\ln x+\ln c\Rightarrow v^{2}+1=\frac{c}{x}$

$\Rightarrow \frac{y^{2}}{x^{2}}+1=\frac{c}{x}\Rightarrow x^{2}+y^{2}=cx$

It pass through (1, 1)

$\therefore$ $x^{2}+y^{2}-2x=0$

Similarly for second differential equation $\frac{dy}{dx}=\frac{2xy}{x^{2}-y^{2}}$

Equation of curve is $x^{2} + y^{2}$ $-$ 2y = 0

Now required area is 


[IMG]


$=2\int\limits _{0}^{1}\left (\sqrt{2x-x^{2}}-x\right )dx$

$=(\frac{π}{2}-1)$ sq. units

text:
Given that the inverse trigonometric functions take principal values only. Then, the number of real values of x which satisfy 

$\sin ^{-1}\left (\frac{3x}{5}\right )+\sin ^{-1}\left (\frac{4x}{5}\right )=\sin ^{-1}x$ is equal to :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 16th March Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\sin ^{-1}\frac{3x}{5}+\sin ^{-1}\frac{4x}{5}=\sin ^{-1}x$

$\sin ^{-1}\left (\frac{3x}{5}\sqrt{1-\frac{16x^{2}}{25}}+\frac{4x}{5}\sqrt{1-\frac{9x^{2}}{25}}\right )=\sin ^{-1}x$

$\frac{3x}{5}\sqrt{1-\frac{16x^{2}}{25}}+\frac{4x}{5}\sqrt{1-\frac{9x^{2}}{25}}=x$

$x=0$ or $3\sqrt{25-16x^{2}}+4\sqrt{25-9x^{2}}=25$

$4\sqrt{25-9x^{2}}=25-3\sqrt{25-16x^{2}}$ 

Squaring we get

$16(25-9x^{2})=625+9(25-16x^{2})-150\sqrt{25-16x^{2}}$

$400=625+225-150\sqrt{25-16x^{2}}$

$\sqrt{25-16x^{2}}=3\Rightarrow 25-16x^{2}=9$

$\Rightarrow x^{2}=1$

Put x = 0, 1, $-$1 in the original equation

We see that all values satisfy the original equation.

Number of solution = 3

text:
Let A($-$1, 1), B(3, 4) and C(2, 0) be given three points. 
A line y = mx, m > 0, intersects lines AC and BC at point P and Q respectively. Let $A_{1}$ and $A_{2}$ be the areas of $\Delta$ABC and $\Delta$PQC respectively, such that $A_{1} = 3A_{2}$, then the value of m is equal to :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 16th March Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)
tags: straight lines and pair of straight lines

solution.body:
Area of triangle ABC:

$A_{1}=\dfrac{1}{2}|(-1)(4-0)+3(0-1)+2(1-4)|=\dfrac{1}{2}|-4-3-6|=\dfrac{13}{2}$

Line AC is $y=-\dfrac{1}{3}(x-2)$; with $y=mx$ it gives $P=\left (\dfrac{2}{3m+1},\dfrac{2m}{3m+1}\right )$.

Line BC is $y=4(x-2)$; with $y=mx$ it gives $Q=\left (\dfrac{8}{4-m},\dfrac{8m}{4-m}\right )$.

Triangles PQC and ABC share the angle at C, with P on line CA and Q on line CB, so

$\dfrac{A_{2}}{A_{1}}=\left |\dfrac{CP}{CA}\right |\cdot \left |\dfrac{CQ}{CB}\right |,\dfrac{CP}{CA}=\dfrac{2-x_{P}}{2-(-1)}=\dfrac{2m}{3m+1},\dfrac{CQ}{CB}=\dfrac{x_{Q}-2}{3-2}=\dfrac{2m}{4-m}$

$A_{1}=3A_{2}$ gives

$\dfrac{4m^{2}}{|(3m+1)(4-m)|}=\dfrac{1}{3}\Rightarrow 12m^{2}=\left |-3m^{2}+11m+4\right |$

The sign $12m^{2}=3m^{2}-11m-4$ gives $9m^{2}+11m+4=0$, which has no real root (discriminant $121-144<0$). The other sign gives

$15m^{2}-11m-4=0\Rightarrow (m-1)(15m+4)=0\Rightarrow m=1\text{or}-\dfrac{4}{15}$

Since $m>0$, $m=1$, with $P=\left (\dfrac{1}{2},\dfrac{1}{2}\right )$ and $Q=\left (\dfrac{8}{3},\dfrac{8}{3}\right )$.

Hence, the correct option is (A).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 16th March Evening Shift

text:
For real numbers $α$, $β$, $γ$ and $δ$, if 
$\int \frac{(x^{2}-1)+\tan ^{-1}\left (\frac{x2+1}{x}\right )}{(x^{4}+3x^{2}+1)\tan ^{-1}\left (\frac{x2+1}{x}\right )}dx$

 $=α\log _{e}\left (\tan ^{-1}\left (\frac{x^{2}+1}{x}\right )\right )+β\tan ^{-1}\left (\frac{γ(x^{2}-1)}{x}\right )+δ\tan ^{-1}\left (\frac{x^{2}+1}{x}\right )+C$ 

where C is an arbitrary constant, then the value of 10($α$ + $βγ$ + $δ$) is equal to $______________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 16th March Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\int \frac{(x^{2}-1)+\tan ^{-1}\left (\frac{x2+1}{x}\right )}{(x^{4}+3x^{2}+1)\tan ^{-1}\left (\frac{x2+1}{x}\right )}dx$

= $\int \frac{x^{2}-1}{(x^{4}+3x^{2}+1)\tan ^{-1}\left (\frac{x2+1}{x}\right )}dx+\int \frac{1}{x^{4}+3x^{2}+1}dx$

Let, $I_{1}=\int \frac{1-\frac{1}{x2}}{\left [\left (x+\frac{1}{x}\right )^{2}+1\right ]\tan ^{-1}\left (x+\frac{1}{x}\right )}dx$

and $I_{2}=\int \frac{dx}{x^{4}+3x^{2}+1}$

$\tan ^{-1}\left (x+\frac{1}{x}\right )=t$

$I_{1}=\int \frac{dt}{t}$

$I_{1}=\ln (t)=\ln \left |\tan ^{-1}\left (x+\frac{1}{x}\right )\right |$

Now

$I_{2}=\int \frac{dx}{x^{4}+3x^{2}+1}$

$=\frac{1}{2}\int \frac{(x^{2}+1)-(x^{2}-1)}{x^{4}+3x^{2}+1}dx$

$=\frac{1}{2}\left [\int \frac{1+\frac{1}{x2}}{x^{2}+3+\frac{1}{x2}}dx-\int \frac{\left (1-\frac{1}{x2}\right )}{x^{2}+3+\frac{1}{x2}}dx\right ]$

$=\frac{1}{2}\left [\int \frac{1+\frac{1}{x2}}{\left [\left (x-\frac{1}{x}\right )^{2}+5\right ]}dx-\int \frac{1-\frac{1}{x2}}{\left [\left (x+\frac{1}{x}\right )^{2}+1\right ]}dx\right ]$

Let $x-\frac{1}{x}=u$ and $x+\frac{1}{x}=v$

$=\frac{1}{2}\left [\int \frac{du}{u^{2}+\left (\sqrt{5}\right )^{2}}-\int \frac{dv}{v^{2}+1}\right ]$

$I_{2}=\frac{1}{2\sqrt{5}}\tan ^{-1}\left (\frac{x-\frac{1}{x}}{\sqrt{5}}\right )-\frac{1}{2}\tan ^{-1}\left (x+\frac{1}{x}\right )$

$I=I_{1}+I_{2}=$

$\ln \left |\tan ^{-1}\left (x+\frac{1}{x}\right )\right |+\frac{1}{2\sqrt{5}}\tan ^{-1}\left (\frac{x^{2}-1}{\sqrt{5}x}\right )-\frac{1}{2}\tan ^{-1}\left (\frac{x^{2}+1}{x}\right )+C$

$α=1,β=\frac{1}{2\sqrt{5}},γ=\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}},δ=-\frac{1}{2}$

$\therefore$ $10(α+βγ+δ)=10\left [1+\frac{1}{10}-\frac{1}{2}\right ]$

$=10\left (\frac{1}{10}+\frac{1}{2}\right )$

$=1+5=6$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 16th March Evening Shift

text:
Let f : R $\to$ R and g : R $\to$ R be defined as 

$f(x)=\left \{\begin{array}{ll} x+a, & x<0 \\ |x-1|, & x\geq 0 \end{array} \right.$ and 

$g(x)=\left \{\begin{array}{ll} x+1, & x<0 \\ (x-1)^{2}+b, & x\geq 0 \end{array} \right.$,

 where a, b are non-negative real numbers. If (gof) (x) is continuous for all x $\in$ R, then a + b is equal to $____________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 16th March Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$g[f(x)]=\left [\begin{array}{ll} f(x)+1 & f(x)<0 \\ (f(x)-1)^{2}+b & f(x)\geq 0 \end{array} \right.$

$g[f(x)]=\left [\begin{array}{ll} x+a+1 & x+a<0&x<0 \\ |x-1|+1 & |x-1|<0&x\geq 0 \\ (x+a-1)^{2}+b & x+a\geq 0&x<0 \\ (|x-1|-1)^{2}+b & |x-1|\geq 0&x\geq 0 \end{array} \right.$

$g[f(x)]=\left [\begin{array}{ll} x+a+1 & x\in (-\infty ,-a)&x\in (-\infty ,0) \\ |x-1|+1 & x\in 𝜙 \\ (x+a-1)^{2}+b & x\in [-a,\infty )&x\in [0,\infty ) \\ (|x-1|-1)^{2}+b & x\in R&x\in [0,\infty ) \end{array} \right.$

$g[f(x)]=\left [\begin{array}{ll} x+a+1 & x\in (-\infty ,-a) \\ (x+a-1)^{2}+b & x\in [-a,0) \\ (|x-1|-1)^{2}+b & x\in [0,\infty ) \end{array} \right.$

g(f(x)) is continuous.

At x = $-$a

$-a + a + 1 = (-a + a - 1)^{2} + b$

$\Rightarrow$ 1 = b + 1

$\Rightarrow$ b = 0

at x = 0

(a $-1)^{2} + b = (|0 - 1| - 1)^{2} + b$

$\Rightarrow$ (a $-1)^{2} + b = b$

$\Rightarrow$ a = 1

$\Rightarrow$ a + b = 1

text:
Consider the statistics of two sets of observations as follows :

  
    
    Size
    Mean
    Variance
  

  
    Observation I
    10
    2
    2
  
  
    Observation II
    n
    3
    1
  

If the variance of the combined set of these two observations is $\frac{17}{9}$, then the value of n is equal to $___________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 16th March Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
For group - 1 : $\frac{\sum x_{i}}{10}=2\Rightarrow \sum x_{i}=20$

$\frac{\sum x_{i}^{2}}{10}-(2)^{2}=2\Rightarrow \sum x_{i}^{2}=60$

For group - 2 : $\frac{\sum y_{i}}{n}=3\Rightarrow \sum y_{i}=3n$

$\frac{\sum y_{i}^{2}}{n}-3^{2}=1\Rightarrow \sum y_{i}^{2}=10n$

Now, combined variance

$σ^{2}=\frac{\sum \left (x_{i}^{2}+y_{i}^{2}\right )}{10+n}-\left (\frac{\sum (x_{i}+y_{i})}{10+n}\right )^{2}$

$\Rightarrow \frac{17}{9}=\frac{60+10n}{10+n}-\frac{(20+3n)^{2}}{(10+n)^{2}}$

$\Rightarrow$ $17 (n^{2} + 20n + 100) = 9(n^{2} + 40n + 200)$

$\Rightarrow$ $8n^{2}$ $-$ 20n $-$ 100 = 0

$\Rightarrow$ $2n^{2}$ $-$ 5n $-$ 25 = 0 $\Rightarrow$ n = 5
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 16th March Evening Shift
